name: RFC 4180
claims: CSV uses quoted fields, doubled quotes, and records separated by line breaks; fields containing delimiter, quotes, or line breaks require quoting.
limitations: CSV implementations vary; RFC 4180 is informational rather than a universal mandatory standard.

name: OWASP CSV Injection
claims: Spreadsheet applications may interpret cells beginning with formula-triggering prefixes as formulas.
limitations: No universal escaping scheme is safe for every spreadsheet workflow; exact preservation and mitigation can conflict.

name: SheetJS CE documentation
claims: SheetJS Community Edition supports browser-side spreadsheet parsing and XLSX generation.
license: Apache-2.0 for SheetJS CE distribution; deployment must pin and review exact package notices.
limitations: CE does not evaluate spreadsheet formulas and complex workbook features may not round-trip perfectly.

name: Microsoft Open XML formulas documentation
claims: Spreadsheet formulas are stored in cell formula elements and cached values may be stored separately.
limitations: Cached values may be stale; extracting formulas is not equivalent to recalculating them.
